paragraphs.source_en: No doubt, that sounds weird - or perhaps you'd say nutty. To be true, not only would H20 molecules in a glass of room-temperature water have to coalesce spontaneously into partially formed cubes of ice, but the digi tal bits in the surveillance camera, as well as the neurons in your brain and those in the brain of the guy across the way, would all need to spontaneously arrange themselves by 1 0: 30 p. m. to attest to there having been a collection of fully formed ice cubes that melted, even though there never was. Yet this bizarre-sounding conclusion is where a faithful application of entropic reasoning- the same reasoning that you embrace without hes itation to explain why the partially melted ice you see at 1 0: 30 p. m. continues to melt toward 1 1 : 00 p. m. -leads when applied in the time-symmetric manner dictated by the laws of physics.
